claims.text: The initial material is equiatomic FeNiCrMn in a single-phase FCC solid-solution state.
The initial crystal is free of pre-existing dislocations and HCP phases.
Local chemical short-range-order clusters may be present in the initial FeNiCrMn crystal.
Yielding is initiated by Shockley partial dislocations nucleating at free surfaces.
The nucleated Shockley partials propagate and form intrinsic stacking faults.
Local SRO clusters act as obstacles or pinning sites for dislocation motion.
The critical stress for partial-dislocation nucleation is orientation-dependent through the Schmid factor.
Lattice friction arises from atomic-size or lattice-parameter mismatch among Fe, Ni, Cr, and Mn.
SRO and atomic-size mismatch hinder partial-dislocation motion more strongly than full-dislocation motion.
The proposed dislocation-friction mechanism prevents twinning and an FCC-to-HCP transformation.
A <11-1>-oriented FeNiCrMn crystal will have a higher macroscopic yield stress than a <110>-oriented crystal.
The higher predicted yield stress in the <11-1> orientation results from its geometric alignment and a higher required stress for partial nucleation.
The observed HCP-like regions are transient intrinsic stacking faults stabilized by SRO rather than a thermodynamic HCP phase.
Stacking-fault regions should show local HCP stacking sequences without long-range chemical ordering or a distinct lattice-parameter shift.
In pure FCC metals, yield strength is primarily controlled by dislocation density and thermal activation rather than HEA-specific SRO and lattice friction.
High-Al AlCoCrFeNi-type compositions can thermodynamically favor BCC-containing or BCC structures.
A distinct lattice-parameter change together with significant elemental segregation would identify the HCP-like region as a stable HCP phase and falsify the stacking-fault interpretation.
An unchanged FCC lattice parameter, a local stacking-sequence change, and no chemical segregation would support identification of the HCP-like region as a stacking fault.

contradictions.description: The structural-mediator and mechanism fields assert free-surface nucleation as the initiating mechanism, while the uncertainty field says the exact nucleation site, including surface versus vacancy cluster, remains speculative.
